summary: Site for an API, SDK, CLI or other developer product: a code-first hero, a quick start with code per step, measured reliability, usage-based pricing with an estimator, a docs landing with search and SDKs, and a changelog. Code samples follow one language choice across the whole site.

pages.purpose: Show a developer the first request and its result in the first screen, how long it takes to get going, how reliable it is and what it costs at their volume.

sections.purpose: One-line promise, install command and a code window with the minimal call, plus what happened to it (a log of the result).
alternatives: media-text: a CLI or desktop tool better shown as a terminal recording
fields: Install command per language / package manager
Minimal code sample per supported language
Result of the sample as a short log or response
Primary action (get API key / sign up) and docs link
sections.notes: Code window: CodeTabs (code-block) with scheme dark and persist, language tabs, a copy button with a polite 'copied' announcement and a clipboard fallback. Code stays selectable text, never an image. A small highlighter is enough (comments, strings, numbers, keywords). Picking a language in any code window switches every sample, the install line and the SDK table site-wide, and is remembered per browser. A live result log should update in an aria-live region.

sections.purpose: Three or four steps from zero to the first working call, each step carrying its own code.
fields: Per step: title, one sentence, code per language
sections.notes: Steps follow the site-wide language choice.

sections.purpose: The guarantees and mechanics a developer cares about (retries, signing, idempotency, limits).
fields: Per feature: icon, title, one technical sentence

sections.purpose: Measured uptime, latency and volume with sources, linking to the status page.
fields: Per figure: value, unit, label, source and period
Link to the public status page
sections.notes: Ledger variant reads like a spec. Only measured numbers.

sections.purpose: Plans plus a volume slider that shows the price of each plan at that volume and lights up the cheapest.
fields: Plans: name, included volume, price per period, overage price, limits

sections.purpose: Limits, data retention, regions, SLAs, migration.
fields: Technical and billing questions with answers

sections.purpose: Get an API key / read the docs.

pages.purpose: Docs landing: find the right guide fast, make the first request in your language and pick an SDK.

sections.purpose: Title and a search field focused with the '/' key.
alternatives: input: a plain search field that submits to the docs search
sections.notes: Show the '/' shortcut with kbd; include a skip link.

sections.purpose: Guides grouped by the job the developer has (receive, send, secure, debug).
alternatives: list-layout: many guides that need filtering
fields: Per guide: title, one line, link

sections.purpose: The first request in the chosen language, copyable.
Every official SDK with its install line, version and status.
fields: Per SDK: language, package name, install command, latest version, maintenance status, repository link
sections.notes: The row for the chosen language is highlighted (read it with useCodeLanguage).

pages.purpose: Latest releases as a version ledger, linking to the full changelog.

sections.purpose: What the changelog covers and the versioning policy.
fields: Versioning / deprecation policy in one line

sections.purpose: Recent releases with version, date, kind badges (feature, improvement, fix, breaking) and short notes.
alternatives: activity-timeline: very short notes without per-release pages
fields: Per release: version, ISO date, kind of each change, change notes, breaking-change upgrade note

sections.purpose: Link to the full changelog / subscribe.
sections.notes: When the product has its own changelog site, see the product-support recipe.

content: Supported languages / runtimes and the install command for each
Minimal working code sample per language and its real output
Quick-start steps with code per language
Measured uptime / latency / volume with source and period
Plans, included volume, overage price and free-tier limits
Docs guide list grouped by job
SDK list with package names, versions and repository links
Release history with versions, dates and breaking changes
Status page URL and support / security contact

styles.name: graphite compact code
styles.why: Neutral graphite with one cool accent dot, dark code windows on a light page, dot-grid hero; reads as a precise tool.

styles.name: dark terminal
styles.why: Infrastructure and CLI tools whose audience lives in a terminal: everything dark, mono numerals, no decorative motion.

pitfalls: Code shown as images or with smart quotes from a word processor; samples must be selectable, copyable and actually run.
Language tabs that only switch one window; one choice should drive every sample, install line and SDK row.
Copy buttons that fail silently where the clipboard API is blocked; provide a fallback and announce the result.
Uptime or latency claims that do not match the public status page.
Usage pricing without a worked example or estimator; developers leave when they cannot predict the bill.
Docs search reachable only by mouse; support '/' to focus, arrows and Enter, and keep a skip link.
Breaking changes buried in release notes without an upgrade note and a date.
